tooltip_popover.title: Parity Algebra and Operations
tooltip_popover.content: Parity defines whether an integer is even (2k) or odd (2k + 1). Addition Rules: Even + Even = Even, Odd + Odd = Even, Even + Odd = Odd. Multiplication Rules: Even * Even = Even, Odd * Odd = Odd, Even * Odd = Even.
tooltip_popover.example: Proof of sum of two odds: (2m + 1) + (2n + 1) = 2(m + n + 1), which is even.

tooltip_popover.title: Expanded Place Value Algebraic Notation
tooltip_popover.content: A 2-digit number 'ab' is expressed as 10a + b. A 3-digit number 'abc' is expressed as 100a + 10b + c. Reversing digits: (10a + b) - (10b + a) = 9(a - b), proving differences are always multiples of 9. 3-digit reversal difference: (100a + 10b + c) - (100c + 10b + a) = 99(a - c), always divisible by 99.
tooltip_popover.example: Reversing Digits Puzzle ACT-5.1: Proving algebraic divisibility by 9.

tooltip_popover.title: Proofs for Standard Divisibility Rules
tooltip_popover.content: Divisibility by 2: 10a + b = 2(5a) + b -> depends solely on unit digit b being even. Divisibility by 4: 100a + (10b + c) = 4(25a) + (10b + c) -> depends on last two digits (10b + c). Divisibility by 3/9: 100a + 10b + c = 99a + 9b + (a + b + c) -> depends on digit sum (a + b + c). Divisibility by 11: Alternating sum difference of odd-place and even-place digits is 0 or multiple of 11.
tooltip_popover.example: 214365 digit sum = 21 (not divisible by 9, so number is not divisible by 9).
